name: Phio Pharmaceuticals Corp.

profile.description: Phio Pharmaceuticals Corp. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing immuno-oncology therapeutics on its proprietary INTASYL self-delivering RNAi platform, co-founded by Nobel laureate Craig Mello. Its lead compound, PH-762, is an intratumoral INTASYL compound that silences PD-1 and completed a 22-patient Phase 1b trial in March 2026; PH-894 targets BRD4. The company has no product revenue, and reports 6 full-time employees.

innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Phio completed its 22-patient Phase 1b trial of PH-762 in March 2026 — a modest clinical milestone, but no product has reached registrational trials or generated revenue [2]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI use was found in company disclosures [3]. Market Share (0/2): Pre-revenue; INTASYL is described as the only self-delivering RNAi technology focused on immuno-oncology, but that is a niche claim, not market leadership [3]. Pipeline (1/2): The company intended to request an FDA meeting in Q3 2026 to define next steps for PH-762, with PH-894 behind it, but no dated pivotal program has been disclosed [2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D spending rose 187% year-over-year in Q2 2026, yet absolute spend is small for an oncology developer and constrained by $13.0M of cash [2][4].
innovation.label: WEAK

inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Phio's stated aim of 'innovative pathways toward a cancer-free future' clearly identifies whom it serves and why, but it is common across oncology biotechs and not yet validated by execution [3]. Community Impact (0/2): None found. Employee Retention (0/2): With 6 employees and the CEO also serving as Chairman, principal executive officer and principal financial officer, there is no meaningful retention data [1][3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No insider purchase evidence found; the company is instead raising capital through a $6.36M at-the-market offering [4].
inspiration.label: WEAK

infrastructure.analysis: LIQUIDITY FLOOR TRIGGERED — Infrastructure = 0. Average daily volume of ~127,100 shares at $0.86 equals roughly $109,000 of daily dollar volume, far below the $1,000,000 floor [1]. Underlying metrics are also weak: no revenue (profit margin not meaningful), ROE of -113.7% and a negative forward P/E of -1.41 (which scores 0) [1]. Cash of $13.0M at June 30, 2026 (down from $21.0M at year-end 2025) funds operations into the second half of 2027 per management [2].
infrastructure.label: WEAK

ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Drug development is gated by clinical trials and FDA approval, so AI cannot substitute for Phio's regulated clinical assets or its patent-protected INTASYL chemistry [2][3]. However, AI-driven siRNA design and target discovery are lowering barriers for well-funded RNAi competitors, which could commoditize platform-level differentiation for a company with only $13.0M of cash and no AI capability of its own [2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI revenue.
ai_resilience.label: MODERATE

infinite_game.summary: Phio has a sincere scientific purpose — harnessing RNAi to help the immune system fight cancer — and has survived more than a decade of pivots, but Sinek would note that its decisions are dictated by its cash runway rather than a Just Cause. A six-person company financing itself through small at-the-market offerings is focused on reaching the next milestone, leaving little room for the long-term courage and trusting-team depth that define infinite players.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): A 'cancer-free future' is idealistic and service-oriented, but it is a common oncology aspiration that has not shaped distinctive strategic choices or been tested through sustained execution [3].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Strategy is constrained by financing — a $6.36M ATM was set up in April 2026 and management requested an FDA meeting rather than committing to a funded next-phase trial [2][4]. No examples of costly long-term bets were found.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): With 6 employees, the CEO concurrently serving as Chairman, principal executive officer and principal financial officer, and a history of leadership turnover before Robert Bitterman took over in 2022-2023, the organization lacks the depth for a Circle of Safety [1][3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The company has refocused its RNAi platform onto immuno-oncology, and Bitterman was brought in to lead a transition from research to product development [3]. The pivot was meaningful but driven as much by survival as by cause.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence of management framing larger RNAi or checkpoint-inhibitor developers as worthy rivals to learn from [3].

investment_thesis: Phio offers high-risk optionality on a differentiated RNAi platform co-founded by Nobel laureate Craig Mello: INTASYL compounds self-deliver into tumors without lipid nanoparticles, and PH-762 (PD-1 silencing) completed a 22-patient Phase 1b study in March 2026 [2][3]. An FDA meeting to define next steps was planned for Q3 2026, and management says cash of $13.0M funds operations into the second half of 2027 [2]. With a market cap near $10M, positive regulatory feedback or a partnership could rerate the shares [1].
thesis_continued: The bear case is severe: Phio has no revenue, cash fell from $21.0M to $13.0M in six months, the Q1 2026 net loss doubled to $4.0M, and the April 2026 ATM of up to $6.36M (about 5.0M shares versus 11.6M outstanding) implies heavy dilution [2][4]. The stock at $0.86 is below Nasdaq's $1 minimum bid, and past filings warn that cumulative reverse splits may eliminate the usual grace period [1][4]. Daily dollar volume of ~$109K is far below IOWN's liquidity floor [1].
key_catalysts: FDA feedback on the PH-762 development path following the Q3 2026 meeting request
Partnership or licensing deal for the INTASYL platform that brings non-dilutive capital
Advancement of PH-894 (BRD4 silencing) toward the clinic
key_risks: Cash runway only into 2H 2027 with ongoing ATM dilution (up to ~5.0M new shares vs. 11.6M outstanding)
Nasdaq delisting risk with the share price below $1.00 and limited reverse-split flexibility
Clinical or regulatory setback for PH-762, the company's only clinical-stage asset
Competition from well-funded RNAi and checkpoint-inhibitor developers using AI-driven design
Illiquidity: ~$109K average daily dollar volume, far below IOWN's $1M floor
